name: Marc Andreessen

summary.text: Marc Andreessen co-wrote the Mosaic browser at the University of Illinois' NCSA in 1992–93, co-founded Mosaic Communications (later Netscape) in 1994, and co-founded Andreessen Horowitz in 2009. He joined Facebook's board in June 2008, when Peter Thiel was already a director, and the two served together until Thiel left the board at Meta's 2022 annual meeting. In July 2024 he endorsed Donald Trump, and Business Insider, citing FEC filings, reported that he gave $2.5 million to the pro-Trump super PAC Right for America. In late 2024 he was reported to be recruiting staff for Elon Musk's DOGE without a formal role, and in March 2026 he was appointed to PCAST, co-chaired by David Sacks and Michael Kratsios.

facts.claim: Andreessen has been reported as an investor in Pronomos Capital, a venture fund that backs 'startup city' or charter-city projects, which had raised at least $13.3 million from backers including Peter Thiel and Andreessen.

sources.title: The New VC Idea That Surely Won't Backfire: Colonies of Tech Bros

facts.claim: In 2014 activist investor Carl Icahn, in letters filed with the SEC, accused eBay director Marc Andreessen of conflicts of interest over the 2009 sale of 70% of Skype to a group including Andreessen's firm, which later profited when Skype was sold to Microsoft. eBay said Andreessen recused himself and that Andreessen Horowitz held about 3% of the buying consortium.

eBay response to Icahn

facts.claim: As an undergraduate and part-time assistant at the National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA), University of Illinois, Andreessen recruited NCSA programmer Eric Bina to build the Mosaic graphical web browser. A Unix version was posted on NCSA's servers in early 1993, followed by PC and Mac versions in late spring 1993.

sources.title: Marc Andreesen and Eric Bina

facts.claim: Mosaic Communications Corp., which became Netscape Communications, was incorporated in Mountain View, California, in mid-1994.

sources.title: Marc Andreesen and Eric Bina

facts.claim: On November 24, 1998, America Online announced it would acquire Netscape Communications in a stock-for-stock transaction valued at $4.2 billion, with Netscape shareholders receiving 0.45 AOL shares per Netscape share.

sources.title: November 24: AOL Buys Netscape

facts.claim: Andreessen and Ben Horowitz announced their support for Donald Trump in the 2024 election in July 2024, framing it around policy toward startups ('little tech'), crypto and AI, and said they would make personal (not firm) contributions to his campaign. Horowitz said: 'for little tech, we think Donald Trump is actually the right choice.'

sources.title: Andreessen Horowitz founders the latest to stake Trump, as tech money piles into his coffers

facts.claim: Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz each gave $2.5 million to Right for America, a super PAC whose stated goal was to ensure Trump's victory in the 2024 election, Business Insider reported, citing FEC filings.

connections.claim: Marc Andreessen co-founded venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Ben Horowitz in 2009. The firm reports more than $100 billion under management across multiple funds.

sources.title: About a16z

connections.claim: Andreessen has served on the board of Facebook (now Meta) since June 2008. In 2016 shareholder litigation in the Delaware Chancery Court, plaintiffs' filings alleged that while serving on the special committee negotiating a new non-voting share class, he privately texted Mark Zuckerberg during the negotiations in ways that coached him, rather than representing shareholders.

connections.claim: Andreessen was reported in January 2020 to be among the backers, alongside Peter Thiel, of JD Vance's Cincinnati-based venture firm Narya Capital, which had raised $93 million.

connections.claim: When Andreessen joined Facebook's board on June 30, 2008, Peter Thiel (of Clarium Capital and Founders Fund) was already a director. The two served together until Thiel retired from the board at Meta's May 25, 2022 annual meeting.

connections.claim: Text messages made public in a late-September 2022 court filing in Twitter's lawsuit against Musk showed Andreessen telling Musk that $250 million was available for his Twitter purchase 'with no additional work required.' Andreessen's firm, AH Capital Management (a16z), committed $400 million in equity to the deal, according to Musk's May 2022 SEC filing.

openQuestions: The Washington Post's original late-November 2024 report on Andreessen's DOGE recruiting was not opened directly; only Fortune's summary of it and of the FT report.
Exact wording of Andreessen's 2022 text to Musk is from secondary coverage (CJR), not the Delaware Chancery exhibit itself.
Andreessen's Fairshake and Leading the Future amounts are FEC 'partnership attribution' memo entries of a16z's management-company contributions, not separate personal checks.
No primary source opened for Andreessen's Netscape titles or the 1995 Netscape IPO; AOL CTO role after the 1999 merger not verified.
Existing summary's '$44 million / $22 million each' Fairshake figure reflects mid-2024 totals; FEC now shows $67 million (2024 cycle) and $33.5 million attributed to each founder.
